chunks: What Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ghalib ibn Uthman, from Rawh ibn Abd al-Rahim, who said:
I asked Abu Abd Allah (AS) about vomiting. He said: 'There is no wudu [required] for it, even if you vomited intentionally.'

key_terms.الْقَيْءِ: vomiting — expulsion of stomach contents; the legal subject of this ruling
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّداً: intentionally — the qualifier extending the ruling even to willful vomiting
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat; ruled here as not obligated by vomiting

ai.seo_question: Does vomiting invalidate wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) categorically rules that vomiting (al-qay') does not nullify wudu in Imami jurisprudence, regardless of whether it was accidental or deliberate. The Imam's qualifier 'even if intentionally' closes any possible ambiguity and distinguishes this position from certain Sunni schools that count vomiting among the nullifiers of ritual purity.
